skill.name: gsap-core
skill.description: Write and review GSAP tweens for DOM and SVG elements. Choose easing and stagger settings, control playback, and adapt animations to screen size and reduced motion preferences.
skill.summary: Create GSAP tweens with responsive behavior and reduced motion support.
skill.author: greensock

content.user_title: Build Responsive Web Animations with GSAP
content.value_statement: Web animations can feel inconsistent across screen sizes and ignore user motion preferences. This skill guides you in writing GSAP tweens with predictable timing, responsive behavior, and reduced motion support.
actual_capabilities: Choose gsap.to(), gsap.from(), gsap.fromTo(), or gsap.set() based on the desired start and end states.
Configure tween duration, easing, stagger order, and project-wide defaults.
Animate DOM and SVG properties using transform aliases, fade visibility, and SVG origin settings.
Calculate animation values per target or relative to current values.
Store tween instances to pause, reverse, or stop playback.
Use gsap.matchMedia() to set up and revert animations at breakpoints and for reduced motion.
limitations: Your project needs GSAP installed or otherwise available to run the examples.
Responsive examples using gsap.matchMedia() require GSAP 3.11 or later.
The skill refers to separate guides for detailed timeline sequencing, scroll-linked animation, and React integration.
Custom easing examples require the separate CustomEase plugin.

use_cases.title: Add a Staggered List Entrance
use_cases.description: Reveal a list of cards with a short transform and fade. Set the interval between each card.

use_cases.title: Prototype SVG Motion
use_cases.description: Rotate several SVG elements around a shared point. Compare built-in easing curves before choosing one.

use_cases.title: Review Reduced Motion Behavior
use_cases.description: Check that content stays visible when motion is disabled. Verify that switching breakpoints reverts the previous animation.

prompt_templates.title: Write a First Tween
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to move [selector] 24 pixels to the right in half a second with GSAP. Explain why you chose that tween method.

prompt_templates.title: Stagger a List Entrance
prompt_templates.prompt: Reveal [item selector] from slightly below with a stagger. Use a built-in ease and explain how to adjust the time between items.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Overlapping Tweens
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these two entrance tweens: [snippet]. Explain when each start state applies and show where to change immediateRender so the first tween stays visible.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Motion Across Breakpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Handle conditions and component cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [animation snippet] with gsap.matchMedia() for desktop, mobile, and reduced motion. Scope selectors to [container] and show how to revert animations on unmount.

output_examples.input: Reveal five cards from the center with a short stagger.
output_examples.output: The center card starts first, followed by the adjacent cards and then the outer cards. Each card fades in while moving a short distance upward.

output_examples.input: Keep a heading visible without movement for users who prefer reduced motion.
output_examples.output: Set the heading to its final visible state without animating it when reduced motion is enabled. Revert the original tween when the preference changes.

best_practices: Use camelCase property names and GSAP transform aliases for motion.
Store the returned tween when you need to control playback later.
Test breakpoint changes and reduced motion with content that remains visible when animation is skipped.
anti_patterns: Avoid animating width or position properties when a transform can produce the same visual result.
Avoid setting both svgOrigin and transformOrigin on the same SVG target.
Avoid leaving immediateRender enabled on later entrance tweens that target the same property before they play.

faq.question: What is the difference between a tween and a timeline?
faq.answer: A tween animates properties over time. A timeline organizes multiple tweens so you can coordinate and control them together.

faq.question: When should I use gsap.fromTo()?
faq.answer: Use it when you need to specify both the starting and ending animation values.

faq.question: Can I animate several elements with one call?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass a selector that matches several elements, an array, or a NodeList. Use stagger to offset their start times.

faq.question: Can I use this skill for SVG animations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SVG transforms and using svgOrigin to rotate or scale elements around a shared point.

faq.question: Can I use these examples in React or Vue?
faq.answer: Yes. Adapt the examples to your component lifecycle and clean up animations when the component unmounts.

faq.question: How do I respect reduced motion preferences?
faq.answer: Use gsap.matchMedia() to check prefers-reduced-motion. Set the final state immediately or skip the animation while keeping content visible.
